issues.title: Missing tri-license header in version.h
issues.description: The rule requires that every .c and .h file in the src/ directory contains a copyright header with the text 'Licensed under your choice of (a) the Redis Source Available License 2.0 (RSALv2); or (b) the Server Side Public License v1 (SSPLv1); or (c) the GNU Affero General Public License v3 (AGPLv3)', but src/version.h lacks this required tri-license header
issues.rule_name: All Source Files Must Include Tri-License Header

issues.title: Active defragmentation incorrectly forced ON after replication sync
issues.description: The code saves the original active_defrag_enabled value but then unconditionally sets it to 1 instead of restoring the original value. This means if active defragmentation was disabled before the replication sync (orig_active_defrag = 0), it will be incorrectly enabled after emptyData() completes. This breaks the intended behavior of preserving the user's defragmentation configuration and can cause unexpected performance degradation or memory operations on replicas that should not have defragmentation running.

issues.title: Stream entries incorrectly marked as referenced when cgroups_ref is NULL
issues.description: When cgroups_ref is NULL (which occurs after DEBUG RELOAD with empty PEL), the function returns 1 indicating the entry IS referenced, when it should return 0 indicating it is NOT referenced. This inverted logic prevents XADD/XTRIM operations with the ACKED strategy from correctly deleting entries that have been fully acknowledged by all consumer groups. The result is a memory leak where stream entries accumulate unnecessarily because they are incorrectly protected from deletion even though no consumer group has them in their pending entry list.

issues.title: Inverted reply discard logic causes test infrastructure failure
issues.description: The condition for discarding replies is inverted - replies are discarded when count is NOT a multiple of frequency (!=), rather than when it IS a multiple (==). This causes the test to read and discard replies at the wrong times, leading to a buffer overflow of unread replies. The discard_replies_every helper is called throughout the test suite after batches of Redis commands to prevent reply buffer buildup. With this bug, replies accumulate in the buffer instead of being cleared, causing test hangs or failures when the client tries to send new commands with a full reply buffer.

issues.title: Unused local variable triggers -Werror build failure
issues.description: The newly introduced local variable `orig_active_defrag` is never used, which will trigger an `-Wunused-variable` warning. With `-Werror`, this becomes a compilation error, violating the rule that the build must compile cleanly with warnings treated as errors.
issues.rule_name: Build Must Compile Without Warnings When -Werror is Enabled

issues.title: Header file lacks required double-underscore include guard
issues.description: `src/version.h` does not define any include guard, violating the requirement that header files use standardized double-underscore include guards (e.g., `#ifndef __VERSION_H__` / `#define __VERSION_H__` / `#endif`).
issues.rule_name: Header Files Must Use Double-Underscore Include Guards

structured_output.summary:
This is the Redis 8.2.1 patch release, bundling three fixes and a release-notes/version bump. It has three functional changes: (1) during a replica's full-sync database flush, active defrag is turned off so it cannot touch a half-emptied dataset; (2) `streamEntryIsReferenced()` gets a NULL guard for `cgroups_ref` to stop a crash after RDB load; (3) the defrag regression test is refactored to use a new `discard_replies_every` helper, plus a new test for the flush case.

The replication change has a real bug: the code saves `orig_active_defrag` and then restores `server.active_defrag_enabled = 1` instead of the saved value. Any replica with `activedefrag no` will have defrag silently switched on after its first full sync. The stream guard fixes the crash but returns "referenced" (1) for a state that means "no PEL entries", so `XADD/XTRIM ... ACKED` can no longer trim entries that were delivered and acknowledged after a reload. The new stream test's final assertion should fail as a result. The test helper `discard_replies_every` in `memefficiency.tcl` has an inverted condition (`!=` instead of `==`), which makes the existing defrag tests block forever reading replies that were never sent. Overall the PR is not mergeable as-is.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Three defects should block merge: the replication flag restore ignores the saved value and changes user config, the stream NULL guard returns the wrong answer and breaks ACKED trimming, and the test helper's inverted condition will hang the defrag test suite. The rest are lower-severity test and release-notes issues.

architecture.overview:
Redis keeps active defragmentation controlled by a single global flag, `server.active_defrag_enabled`, which the defrag timer checks each tick (`activeDefragTimeProc` in src/defrag.c stops a running cycle if the flag is cleared). On the replica side, `rdbLoadEmptyDbFunc()` in src/replication.c flushes the old dataset with `emptyData()` before loading the master's RDB, and calls `replicationEmptyDbCallback()`, which calls `processEventsWhileBlocked()`. That lets timers, including defrag, run mid-flush. Streams track consumer-group pending entries in two indexes: `cgroups` (groups) and `cgroups_ref` (message ID to groups that hold it in their PEL). `streamEntryIsReferenced()` consults both to decide whether `ACKED` trimming can delete an entry.

This PR touches three of those seams. It wraps the flush in a defrag-disable/restore pair, adds a NULL guard in front of the `cgroups_ref` lookup, and adds regression tests for both. It also updates the release notes and version string. The flush wrapper's restore step does not put back the value it saved, and the stream guard's return value contradicts how the rest of the function treats an empty PEL.
steps: Entry point: a replica receives a full-sync RDB, and `rdbLoadEmptyDbFunc()` in src/replication.c calls `emptyData()` to flush the old data. Defrag can run during the flush because `replicationEmptyDbCallback()` processes events while blocked.

Change 1: the PR sets `server.active_defrag_enabled = 0` before the flush and restores it afterwards. Because `activeDefragTimeProc` checks this flag, an in-flight cycle is stopped on its next tick. The restore step is the broken part: it writes 1 instead of the saved value.

Change 2: `streamEntryIsReferenced()` in src/t_stream.c is called by `ACKED` trimming in `XADD`/`XTRIM`/`XDELEX`. The PR adds `if (!s->cgroups_ref) return 1;`, which prevents the NULL dereference in `raxFind`. Its effect on trimming is what needs checking.

Change 3: a new test in tests/unit/type/stream.tcl runs `DEBUG RELOAD` twice and expects `ACKED` trimming to work after the PEL has emptied. In the flow the test describes, the first reload leaves `cgroups_ref` NULL, so the guard's return value determines the outcome.

Change 4: tests/unit/memefficiency.tcl gets a `discard_replies_every` helper and a new flush-vs-defrag test. The helper is shared by several existing defrag tests, so its condition errors affect the whole defrag suite.
Housekeeping: `version.h` moves to 8.2.1 and the release notes gain an 8.2.1 section. The notes also list #14240, which is not part of this PR's description.

diagrams.description: Traces how the new NULL guard sits inside the reference check used by ACKED trimming.

findings.title: Defrag flag restored to 1 instead of the saved value
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/replication.c`, `rdbLoadEmptyDbFunc()` saves `orig_active_defrag` (around line 1956) but restores `server.active_defrag_enabled = 1` (around line 1962). Change the restore to write back the saved `orig_active_defrag` value so that a replica with `activedefrag no` keeps defrag disabled after a full sync. Keep the disable step before `emptyData()` unchanged.

findings.title: NULL cgroups_ref guard returns 'referenced' and blocks ACKED trimming
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/t_stream.c`, `streamEntryIsReferenced()` (around line 2708) adds `if (!s->cgroups_ref) return 1;` to avoid a NULL dereference. Change it to `return 0`. A NULL `cgroups_ref` means no consumer group PEL holds the message, so the entry is not referenced and `ACKED` trimming may delete it. Also confirm that `tests/unit/type/stream.tcl` (the test starting near line 247, last assertion near line 271) passes with this change. Keep the existing `cgroups` empty and min-last-id checks as they are.

findings.title: Inverted condition in discard_replies_every helper hangs the defrag tests
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/unit/memefficiency.tcl`, the `discard_replies_every` proc (around lines 70-76) uses `if {$count % $frequency != 0}`. It must be `== 0` to match the original inline `if {$count % 10000 == 0}` pattern it replaces at each call site. Fix the comparison only. Callers pass `(rd, count, 10000, N)` and should not need changes.

findings.title: Replica flush test passes vacuously when defrag is unavailable
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/unit/memefficiency.tcl`, the new test 'Active defrag can't be triggered during replicaof database flush' (starting near line 945) skips silently when `config set activedefrag yes` fails (around line 982-983). Gate the test on jemalloc the same way `test_active_defrag` does (`string match {*jemalloc*} [s mem_allocator]`, or use `tags`/skip logic), and assert that the config set succeeded instead of swallowing the error with `catch`.

findings.title: Release notes list #14240, which is not in this PR
findings.body:
The 8.2.1 release notes list `#14240 INFO KEYSIZES ...`, but the PR description covers only #14274, #14276, the RediSearch fixes, and the LeanVec/LVQ change. #14240 is not part of this diff and does not appear in its description. The notes should match what the release actually ships, so either this entry should be removed or the PR description should say why it is included.

::diff{file="00-RELEASENOTES" lines="22-40"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `00-RELEASENOTES`, the new 8.2.1 section (around lines 22-40) lists `#14240 INFO KEYSIZES ...`, which is not part of this PR's described changes. Confirm with the release owner whether #14240 belongs in 8.2.1. If it does not, remove that bullet. If it does, add the corresponding change to the PR description. Keep the `#Qn` prefix convention that the legend defines.

findings.title: Version bump and release notes are consistent
findings.body: `src/version.h` moves from 8.2.0 to 8.2.1 with the matching `REDIS_VERSION_NUM` of `0x00080201`, and the release notes gain a new 8.2.1 section above the 8.2 GA entry, using the same format and urgency levels defined at the top of the file. The added comment line in `version.h` is harmless. The `#Q` prefixes match the legend.

findings.title: Stream regression test targets the crash path
findings.body: The new test in tests/unit/type/stream.tcl exercises the exact state that caused the crash: an entry is read, the server is reloaded, and `ACKED` trimming runs against the rebuilt reference index. It also covers the empty-PEL reload. The bug is in the return value, not in the choice of scenario, so once the guard is fixed this test should be a useful regression guard. The XACK index extraction (`lindex` nesting) is correct for the `XREADGROUP` reply shape.

findings.title: Flush-time defrag disable covers the synchronous path
findings.body: Disabling `active_defrag_enabled` around `emptyData()` works for the synchronous flush because `replicationEmptyDbCallback()` runs `processEventsWhileBlocked()`. That lets `activeDefragTimeProc` see the cleared flag and call `endDefragCycle(0)`. The approach is sound once the restore step uses the saved value. Note that with `repl_slave_lazy_flush` (`EMPTYDB_ASYNC`), the callback may run after the flag is restored, so the protection does not hold on that path. This is a trade-off worth a comment, not a blocker.
